NovaBio Pharmaceuticals - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBio Pharmaceuticals Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by your name. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBio Pharmaceuticals' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Alex Harper, Chief Executive Officer; Jennifer Patel, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Medical Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Alex Harper, CEO of NovaBio Pharmaceuticals.

Dr. Alex Harper, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBio Pharmaceuticals delivered another strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust volume growth in our flagship GLP-1 receptor agonist NovaGLP-45, continued momentum in oncology from OncoTarget-78, and meaningful regulatory milestones across our portfolio. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including advancing revenue guidance amid key pipeline catalysts, securing regulatory approvals and label expansions, expanding our geographic revenue footprint with emphasis on emerging markets, and executing value-accretive business development through licensing, acquisitions, and partnerships.

We are particularly excited about NovaGLP-45 and its potential to capture substantial share in the obesity and type 2 diabetes markets as we approach critical PDUFA dates and trial readouts.

Now, I will turn the call over to Jennifer, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Jennifer Patel, CFO:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $920 million, an increase of 32% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by 48% volume growth in NovaGLP-45, which continues to gain traction in the oral GLP-1 segment, alongside 38% growth in oncology from OncoTarget-78 and contributions from immunology assets like NovaDerm.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $145 million, or $1.12 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $195 million, or $1.51 per share.

Our operating expenses were $460 million, reflecting continued investment in R&D to support our expanding pipeline while maintaining discipline on G&A. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to fuel innovation across GLP-1s, ADCs, bispecifics, and gene therapies. Our cash position remains strong at $2.9 billion, bolstered by recent business development inflows.

Let me now provide more color on our geographic revenue breakdown, with a particular emphasis on the robust growth in emerging markets, which has become a key pillar of our long-term strategy in the biopharma space.

For the full year to date through Q3 2024, NovaBio has delivered total net product sales approaching $2.4 billion, up approximately 27% on a reported basis and 29% at constant exchange rates. This growth stems from strong volume expansion across our core franchises—oncology, immunology, GLP-1s, and gene therapies—despite some pricing pressures in mature markets. Geographically, our revenue mix shows the maturation of our ex-U.S. presence, now at about 41% of total sales, up from 37% last year. This evolution underscores our globalization efforts as U.S. volumes stabilize post-initial blockbuster ramps.

In the U.S., which accounts for 56% of year-to-date sales or roughly $1.35 billion, growth is led by sustained demand for NovaLumab, our PD-1 inhibitor generating about $950 million year-to-date, up 8% year-over-year even with biosimilar competition from players like Amgen. Label expansions into adjuvant NSCLC and melanoma have boosted patient starts by 13%, though average selling prices dipped 2.5% due to PBM rebates and 340B programs, consistent with trends at Merck and Bristol Myers Squibb.

Europe contributes 24% or $575 million, with sales up 7% at constant rates to around €530 million equivalent. Tender successes in Germany and Italy for biosimilars like our adalimumab follow-on NovaTrafil, now at 19% share in TNF inhibitors, drove this, offsetting flat-to-down 1.5% ASPs from HTA scrutiny by NICE and IQWiG. New launches, including a bispecific for rheumatoid arthritis, added 10% volume growth.

The rest of world, at 20% or $480 million, surged 30% at constant rates, our fastest-growing segment. Emerging markets make up 68% of ROW—14% globally—and exploded 45% to $330 million year-to-date. Our EM strategy leverages organic launches, partnerships, and local manufacturing to address rising chronic disease burdens.

In China, 46% of EM sales at $150 million and up 58% year-over-year, NRDL inclusions for NovaLumab and NovaGLP-1 under VBP rounds propelled 70% volume surges post-launch, at ASPs about 24% of U.S. levels. Our expanded Shanghai facility with WuXi Biologics cut lead times 32%.

India and Southeast Asia, 24% of EM at $80 million up 40%, saw biosimilars like trastuzumab gain 23% HER2 share via Dr. Reddy's and Cipla partnerships, with hepatitis C up 47% in Indonesia and Vietnam from screening initiatives.

Latin America and MENA, 19% at $65 million up 35%, navigated Brazil's CMED controls with NovaLumab winning 62% of oncology bids; Mexico and Saudi Arabia patient programs drove 27% immunology uptake amid Vision 2030.

Other EM like South Africa and Turkey added $35 million up 52% from insulin access.

We've committed $120 million year-to-date in CapEx to EM hubs in Hyderabad, Suzhou, and São Paulo for localization, boosting ANDA/biosimilar approvals to 72%. IP enforcement against 16 infringers preserves value. We see EM growing 32-37% in 2025, ahead of IQVIA's 13-16% biopharma consensus, fueled by catalysts like NovaGLP-1 China readout and Sinopharm combos, with 86% EM gross margins providing buffer against FX and tenders.

Next, I'd like to highlight our pivotal regulatory progress this quarter, where we notched three major wins: FDA full approval for OncoTarget-3, our PD-L1/CD137 bispecific T-cell engager, in frontline metastatic NSCLC; EMA label expansion for NovaDerm, our IL-4/IL-13 inhibitor, into adolescents 12-17 with atopic dermatitis; and NMPA approval for HemoCure, our AAV8 gene therapy for hemophilia B. These unlock about $1.3 billion in incremental peak sales over five years, with Q1 2025 revenue ramps.

OncoTarget-3 earned FDA approval September 15th for frontline NSCLC with platinum chemo, from the 1,024-patient TARGET-LUNG Phase 3 across 187 global sites. Median PFS was 14.2 months versus 9.8 for pembrolizumab plus chemo—a 45% risk reduction, HR 0.55, p<0.0001. ORR reached 68% with 22% CRs, strong in PD-L1-low patients. Confirmatory OS trends positive, median not reached vs. 18.7 months. This converts prior accelerated approval, eyeing 16-21% U.S. frontline NSCLC share, eroding Keytruda's 44% per IQVIA. U.S. peak $475 million by 2028; EMA PRIME decision Q2 2025, PMDA H1 2025, NMPA Q4 2025. NSCLC cases: 230k U.S., 450k EU, 1M China by 2025. Our PD-L1 CDx accelerates uptake like Libtayo in SCC.

NovaDerm, with $2.4 billion global sales last year akin to Dupixent, got EMA CHMP nod October 10th for 12+ AD from AD-TEEN Phase 3 (n=412): EASI-75 72% vs. 19% placebo at week 16, sustained to 52 weeks, safety matching adults—no new signals, anaphylaxis <0.5%. Targets $3.2 billion EU adolescent AD market. U.S. sNDA year-end using RESOLVE RWE (5,200 patient-years), per FDA guidance, approval mid-2025. Pediatric penetration deepens 26%; China Q3 NMPA with Sinopharm launches Q4.

HemoCure NMPA approval September 28th, second in China after Voxzogo. HEMO-B Phase 2/3: 42% Factor IX at 5 years (n=38), ABR down 92%, no toxicity or redosing, better than Hemlibra durability. RMB 2.9 million ($410k) dose, 220 patients Year 1 on NRDL push for 16k patients. U.S. BLA Q1 2025 post-CMC, EMA Q3 2025. Global peak $375 million by 2029, 42% Greater China.

These add $650 million to 2025 guidance, to $6.0-6.4 billion up 20% midpoint. Margins up 320 bps to 83% on biologics. Four new Breakthrough designations; 27% label success vs. 18% industry. Q4 filings: OncoTarget-3 adjuvant, NovaDerm U.S. pediatric. De-risks $16 billion pipeline, raises 3-year EPS CAGR to 23%.

Turning to business development, a cornerstone of our strategy. In Q3, we closed key licensing deals, a tuck-in acquisition, and partnership expansions in ADCs, bispecifics, and gene editing, derisking the pipeline and boosting non-dilutive funding to 27-32% of revenues over five years, from 19% end-2023.

We in-licensed global ex-China rights to BNT-ADC-301, a HER2-low breast cancer ADC from SinoBiotech, Phase IIb with H1 2025 data showing 46% ORR in pretreated patients, rivaling Enhertu. $360 million upfront, $1.25 billion milestones, royalties 19-25%. Bridging study under Project Orbis.

We out-licensed ex-U.S./EU rights to BNT-777, PD-1/VEGF bispecific Phase III NSCLC, to Takeda: $210 million upfront, $825 million milestones, 21-26% royalties. Peak ex-U.S./EU $1.6 billion by 2030 on Asia NSCLC rise. Q3 inflows $580 million, pro forma cash $3.0 billion.

Acquired AuraGenix for $700 million: CRISPR-Cas13a for ALS/Huntington's. AGX-201/202 IND-ready, 72-87% efficiency in iPSCs, low off-targets beating Beam. $470 million upfront, $230 million CVRs on 2026 Phase I. Integrates AI platform cutting timelines 20%; 4.6x sales multiple.

Asia-Pacific 36% partnered potential via NMPA ADC fast-tracks (16+ since 2022); EMA PRIME for BNT-ADC-301; U.S. 62% trials. Merck IO combo Phase II BNT-777/Keytruda 63% 12-month PFS, Phase III basket triggers $155 million, $310 million more targets. Roche/Genentech IL-23/IL-17 psoriasis Phase I, $105 million joint, 61/39 split.

Pillars: pipeline diversification amid Keytruda 2028 cliff; geo derisking vs. IRA; tech efficiency like Recursion. 13 active discussions, two more deals by year-end, $1.2-1.7 billion value. Total milestones >$8.5 billion across 16 programs; 22-27% peak sales CAGR to 2035.

Finally, our outlook for year-end and 2025, with updated revenue guidance and catalysts positioning us for sustained growth.

Building on Q3's $920 million—32% up YoY from NovaGLP-45's 48% volumes—we raise full-year 2024 guidance to $3.05-$3.15 billion, 28-32% over 2023. U.S. 73% or $2.23-$2.30 billion on GLP-1 megatrend to $105 billion by 2030 per IQVIA; Europe 17% $515-$535 million post-EMA/pricing in Germany/France at 16% above forecasts; EM 10% $305-$315 million, China +62% QoQ via Sinopharm.

Oncology 23% Q3 at $210 million, up 37% from OncoTarget-78; full-year $750-$780 million, 34% up on gastric label/EU tenders.

Core growth 26% Q3; margins 83-85% from Singapore efficiencies, semaglutide analog patent expiry.

Near-term catalysts: October 15 PDUFA NovaGLP-45 subQ obesity monotherapy, SURMOUNT-3 22.5% loss vs. 2.4% placebo, GI 17%; peak $4.7 billion vs. Zepbound. Late-November OncoTarget-78 NSCLC DESTINY-Lung04 topline, 1,200 patients, PFS HR 0.54-0.64 for accel approval.

H1 2025: NovaBispec-12 MM interim, MAGNETIS-5 Phase 2/3, Phase 1 93% ORR/69% CR; peak $2.2-3.2 billion in $26 billion market. Roche PROTAC KRAS CRC co-dev, $520 million upfront, SynGenix AI cuts timelines 42% on 52 million pairs.

Longer-term: long-acting GLP-1/GIP monthly Phase 2 for adherence; precision oncology with 3 ADCs/2 bispecifics in $52 billion ADC market 26% CAGR; NC continuous synthesis cuts COGS 22%.

Navigating IRA 5% ASP 2026 hit offset by $1.3 billion buyback; EU HTA aids launches; China JV ahead of generics.

This guidance and catalysts mark our shift to multi-product leader, 22%+ CAGR to 2027, R&D 17% revenues.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to net product revenues of $3.05 billion to $3.15 billion at the midpoint, incorporating these regulatory and BD tailwinds.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Alex.

Dr. Alex Harper, CEO:
Thank you, Jennifer. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jane Doe, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Jennifer, you detailed the upcoming PDUFA for NovaGLP-45's subcutaneous formulation in obesity. Could you elaborate on the SURMOUNT-3 data, competitive positioning against Zepbound and Wegovy, and how this factors into your raised guidance?

Jennifer Patel, CFO:
Thanks, Jane. Absolutely, the SURMOUNT-3 pivotal trial hit both primary endpoints with impressive 22.5% mean weight loss at 72 weeks compared to just 2.4% on placebo, and importantly, a favorable safety profile with gastrointestinal events at only 18% incidence—below the class average. This positions NovaGLP-45 squarely against Eli Lilly's Zepbound and Novo Nordisk's semaglutide offerings, especially as our oral segment already holds about 13% U.S. share competitive with Rybelsus. If approved on October 15th PDUFA, we project peak U.S. sales exceeding $4.5 billion, directly contributing to the midpoint uplift in our full-year guidance and setting up 2025 acceleration. Dr. Singh can add on the clinical nuances if needed.

Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Medical Officer:
Yes, Jane, from a medical perspective, the clean profile and monotherapy efficacy address key adherence gaps in the GLP-1 space, where real-world data shows 40% discontinuation rates. We're confident in broad labeling.

Operator:
Our next question comes from John Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

John Smith, Morgan Stanley:
Great, thanks. On emerging markets, the growth numbers are impressive, especially China. Can you discuss the Sinopharm partnership dynamics, NRDL progress for new assets, and any FX or pricing risks you're modeling?

Dr. Alex Harper, CEO:
John, thanks for the question. Jennifer covered the geo breakdown well—China's 62% QoQ prescription growth for NovaGLP-45 post-NMPA is a testament to our Sinopharm JV, which not only ramps volumes but localizes supply via Shanghai expansions, cutting costs and risks. NRDL inclusions under recent VBP rounds for NovaLumab and GLP-1 analogs have been game-changers, with ASPs at a quarter of U.S. but volumes exploding 70%. We're modeling 30-35% EM growth next year, ahead of peers, with hedges on 8-10% FX volatility and tender pricing, buffered by 85% margins and diversified franchises like oncology tenders in Brazil.

Jennifer Patel, CFO:
To add, John, our tech transfer hubs ensure compliance with local policies like Dual Circulation, and pipeline catalysts like the H1 2025 NovaGLP-1 readout will sustain momentum.

Operator:
Our next question from Mike Johnson with J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson, J.P. Morgan:
Thanks. On the BD front, the AuraGenix acquisition and Roche PROTAC deal sound transformative. How do these integrate with your SynGenix AI platform, and what's the updated milestone runway?

Jennifer Patel, CFO:
Mike, excellent question. AuraGenix's Cas13a RNA editing slots perfectly into our rare disease push, with 70-85% efficiencies in ALS models enhancing our CRISPR capabilities. SynGenix, already slashing lead optimization by 40% via generative AI on 50 million compounds, now incorporates their AlphaFold3 models for 20% further acceleration. Roche's $500 million-plus for KRAS PROTAC taps this, with total milestones now over $8 billion across 16 programs. Expect two more announcements by year-end, funding bolt-ons without dilution.

Dr. Alex Harper, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBio Pharmaceuticals Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
